result.headline: Actuator ch[5] froze at 1500 us from t=73.43 s; control degradation after it is not proven to follow.
result.explanation: The only output that was moving and then froze is actuator ch[5] (from 73.43 s to the end). Roll and yaw tracking worsened after it, but the setpoints also became more aggressive, so cause is not separable.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[5]] held 1500 from t=73.43 to 144.345 s (215 samples)
evidence.shows: One output froze at neutral to the end of the recording with no mode change or event, while ch[1] to ch[4] kept moving.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a10 t=73.43 s: actuator.output[ch[5]] was moving, then held 1500 for 70.915 s (see line 25; strength 4.642)
evidence.shows: Strongest ranked candidate. Before 73.43 s the spread was 17.0 us; after it, 0.0.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.858 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A start-up sensor-health error and a low-voltage warning at 0.858 s. Nothing changed later that points back to them.

checked.check: Compare all series before and after t=73.43 s
checked.result: ch[5] froze (spread 17.0 to 0.0). Yaw tracking error rose 2.883 to 13.049 deg and roll 1.614 to 6.688 deg. Pitch was nearly unchanged (0.451 to 0.712). Yaw and roll setpoint levels and spread also changed.

checked.check: Sequence of signals leaving baseline from 70 to 92 s
checked.result: Roll setpoint left baseline first (70.111 s), then yaw setpoint, ch[3], roll attitude, and so on. ch[1] left at 73.43 s. ch[5] is not listed because it was already at its held value.
Only 2 events, both at start-up (0.858 s). No earlier case matches.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[roll] at t=87.747 s: -49.994 -> 24.465 deg (step 74.459, 6.6x its usual variation)
effects.why: Follows the roll setpoint step of 82.37 deg at 86.735 s (line 52). This looks like a manoeuvre, not a fault.

effects.quote: SHIFT vehicle.velocity[x] changed level for good at t=12.217 s: median 15.795 before, -7.42 after m/s (7.2x its variation before)
effects.why: Velocity swings repeat (lines 64 to 69), so these are manoeuvres, not a lasting fault.

next_action.action: Identify which control surface or function ch[5] drives
next_action.why: A frozen output only matters if it serves an active control loop. This decides whether the freeze explains the roll and yaw tracking change.
how: Read the servo or mixer output mapping for channel 6 (index 5) in the flight controller parameters.
Check the controller's own log for output disable or failsafe around the freeze time (not in this recording).

outcomes.label: ch[5] drives roll or yaw surface
outcomes.means: The frozen output is a plausible main cause of the degraded roll and yaw tracking.
outcomes.then: Check the command feeding ch[5] in the full controller log

outcomes.label: ch[5] is an unused or auxiliary output
outcomes.means: The freeze is likely benign. The tracking change is more likely manoeuvre severity.
outcomes.then: Compare tracking error against setpoint rate in manoeuvres

unknowns: What ch[5] controls, and whether it was commanded neutral or stopped updating.
Whether the roll and yaw tracking change comes from the freeze or from more aggressive setpoints after the freeze.
Why airspeed and yaw_rate are constant 0 (sensor not fitted, or a dead sensor).

already_answered.question: Did a control fault occur, and when?
already_answered.answer: The one output that froze is ch[5] at t=73.43 s. It is a candidate, not a confirmed fault.
already_answered.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[5]] held 1500 from t=73.43 to 144.345 s (215 samples)

already_answered.question: Were there warnings or errors logged?

data_requests.what: Full controller log with output-disable or failsafe state, and the servo function mapping
data_requests.window: Whole flight, especially around the freeze time
data_requests.why_needed: Shows whether ch[5] was commanded neutral or frozen, and what it controls.

unobservable.fact: Physical state of the ch[5] servo, linkage and wiring
unobservable.why_it_matters: The recorded output is a command, so it cannot show whether the surface actually moved.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Bench-test the servo and inspect the linkage and connector.

hypotheses.claim: The ch[5] output stopped following its command at 73.43 s and degraded roll or yaw control.
hypotheses.because: It is the only output that moved and then froze, with no event. Its effect on tracking is unproven.

hypotheses.claim: Setpoints became more aggressive after the freeze, so the larger tracking error is normal behaviour.
hypotheses.because: Roll and yaw setpoint levels and spread rose in the same window as the error. The setpoints moved first.

hypotheses.claim: Airspeed and yaw_rate are constant 0 and a start-up sensor-health error was logged, so estimation may be impaired.
hypotheses.because: Constant zeros for the whole recording point to missing or dead channels. Nothing changed at the freeze time.

hypotheses.claim: A low battery voltage caused the output to stop.
hypotheses.because: The warning is at start-up only. No other output changed at the freeze, and ch[1] to ch[4] kept moving.

events.what: ch[5] output frozen at 1500 us from 73.43 s
events.why: Output was moving, then held to the end with no event.

events.what: Low voltage warning and sensor-health error at 0.858 s

result.lesson: No earlier case is in the workspace.
result.reuse_when: Another airframe where a servo output channel holds a constant neutral value mid-flight with no mode or failsafe event, and that channel drives an active attitude loop.
